name: Drive Like Jehu
label: Headhunter
lede: Drive Like Jehu made two albums, split without telling anyone, and came back 19 years later for a free afternoon in front of a pipe organ in Balboa Park.

eras.title: Two San Diego bands become one
eras.text: Rick Froberg and John Reis spent four years in Pitchfork while Mike Kennedy and Mark Trombino played in Night Soil Man. Both bands ended in 1990, and the four of them started over together.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pitchfork (band) · Wikipedia: Drive Like Jehu
years.h: Froberg and Reis start Pitchfork in San Diego
years.p: Froberg sings and draws the art, Reis plays guitar. The band puts out the three-song Saturn Outhouse EP in 1989 and one album, Eucalyptus, on Nemesis in 1990.
years.xp:
The lineup around them was bassist Don Ankrom (later replaced by Nick Frederick) and drummer Joey Piro. Pitchfork ended in 1990, and Swami Records, Reis's own label, later put both releases on one CD in 2003.

Across town, Mike Kennedy and Mark Trombino spent 1987 to 1990 in a band called Night Soil Man. The two pairs were about to be one band.

years.cap: John Reis at a basement show in the San Fernando Valley
years.src: Wikipedia: Drive Like Jehu · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Reis starts a band named for a chariot-driving king
years.p: He pulls in Froberg and bassist Kennedy, with Chris Bratton on drums. The name comes from Jehu, the chariot driver of the Bible.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Reis formed the band in August 1990, the same year Pitchfork and Night Soil Man both broke up and the year he also started [[Rocket from the Crypt|e297ecdf-64ec-4e34-899d-80380f5b0c2a]]. Bratton was the first drummer.

He did not last: Wikipedia says it simply "didn't work out," and Trombino took the stool, completing the lineup that made both records.

years.cap: Flyer for Drive Like Jehu, Germbox and Power Dresser at the Che Cafe, San Diego
years.h: Mark Trombino takes the drum stool from Bratton
years.p: Trombino, ex-Night Soil Man, drums on every Drive Like Jehu record.

eras.title: A debut on Cargo, a 7-inch on Merge
eras.text: Reis releases two bands' first albums in the same year. Drive Like Jehu's comes with Froberg's drawing on the sleeve.

q: All the music is designed for maximum physical gratification.
years.src: Wikipedia: Drive Like Jehu (album) · San Diego Reader: Drive Like Jehu
years.h: Drive Like Jehu comes out with Froberg's art on the sleeve
years.p: Nine songs in about 45 minutes, recorded at Westbeach Recorders in Los Angeles with producer Donnell Cameron and released on Cargo and Headhunter.
years.xp:
AllMusic's Ned Raggett wrote that the two guitarists sound like they've been "dipped in battery acid, wired to a power station, and let absolutely loose." Wikipedia counts nine tracks and a running time of 44:56.

Froberg's line on the band, to the San Diego Reader: the music is built for physical payoff.

years.h: Reis releases two bands' debuts in the same year
years.p: Rocket from the Crypt's Paint as a Fragrance comes out alongside Drive Like Jehu's album.

years.h: Merge releases a 7-inch with "Hand Over Fist" and "Bullet Train to Vegas"
years.p: Also in 1992, "Sinews" appears on the Head Start to Purgatory compilation from Cargo and Headhunter.

eras.title: Interscope pays for it, then it stops
eras.text: Yank Crime is the last record. Touring it across the US and Europe is the last thing the band does.

years.src: Wikipedia: Yank Crime · Magnet: Lost Classics, Drive Like Jehu Yank Crime · Treble: Drive Like Jehu, Yank Crime
yt: Live at The Rivoli, Toronto, June 14, 1994
years.h: Yank Crime is the second album, and Interscope pays for it
years.p: Recorded at Westbeach Recorders and Big Fish Studios, it opens with "Here Come the Rome Plows" in 5/4.
years.xp:
Interscope had signed both of Reis's bands. Magnet's version: Rocket from the Crypt "erupted" and the label offered "ridiculous amounts of money" to both bands. Treble reports Reis saying Interscope wanted Drive Like Jehu on its own.

Magnet also says Yank Crime and Rocket from the Crypt's three major-label records "proved to be money pits" for the label. Rolling Stone later ranked it number 16 on its list of the 40 greatest emo albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rick Froberg · Wikipedia: Yank Crime
years.h: Froberg draws every Drive Like Jehu sleeve
years.p: He also did the artwork for Rocket from the Crypt and Swami Records.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Froberg entry calls him the illustrator and designer across his bands' releases, including artwork for Rocket from the Crypt and Swami Records. In 2025 Akashic Books published a book of his art, Plenty for All.

q: I equate building tension with repetition.
years.src: Treble: Drive Like Jehu, Yank Crime · Wikipedia: Yank Crime
years.h: "Luau" runs about nine minutes, and Rob Crow sings the back half
years.p: Pinback's [[Rob Crow|bd55048b-137d-46cf-845d-604a51b5ade1]] guests on vocals. Treble calls the song the album's centerpiece.
years.xp: Treble also quotes Reis on certain notes that "rub against each other," which is the part of the band's method a fan can hear on the record. The song is built from interwoven guitar riffs that repeat and climb.

years.src: Wikipedia: Drive Like Jehu · Consequence: The Strange Return of Drive Like Jehu · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Drive Like Jehu just stops, with no announcement
years.p: The last tour is Yank Crime across the US and Europe. Reis's other band, Rocket from the Crypt, is on Interscope with Scream, Dracula, Scream! the same year.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band "disbanded in 1995 without an official announcement." Consequence writes that the members' "disparate interests" pulled them apart. Rocket from the Crypt's "On a Rope" reached number 12 on the UK Singles Chart that year.

years.h: Froberg moves to New York, and Trombino starts producing
years.p: Kennedy becomes a chemist. Trombino goes on to record Blink-182 and Jimmy Eat World, per Wikipedia and Consequence; Froberg plays briefly in Thingy before turning to visual art.

eras.title: Everybody scatters, the records don't
eras.text: Reis and Froberg go back to work as Hot Snakes, Trombino moves to the mixing desk, and younger bands keep citing the records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hot Snakes · Consequence: The Strange Return of Drive Like Jehu
years.h: Froberg and Reis are back together as [[Hot Snakes|dfa0e21c-ee3e-44da-81d5-58e3c1218a9f]]
years.p: Their first album, Automatic Midnight, comes out on Reis's Swami Records. Three studio albums (2000, 2002, 2004) later, Hot Snakes break up in 2005.
years.xp: Consequence dates the reunion to 1999 and calls Hot Snakes the pair's third project together, after Pitchfork and Drive Like Jehu.

years.src: Wikipedia: Drive Like Jehu · Wikipedia: Yank Crime
years.h: Swami reissues Yank Crime with the 7-inch and "Sinews" added
years.p: The magazine Pitchfork scored the reissue 9.0.

years.cap: Hot Snakes (Rick Froberg and John Reis) at Bar Pink, San Diego, November 4, 2011
years.src: Wikipedia: Drive Like Jehu · Consequence: The Strange Return of Drive Like Jehu
years.h: Deftones cover Drive Like Jehu's "Caress"
years.p: Wikipedia lists At the Drive-In, Botch, Modest Mouse and The Dillinger Escape Plan among the bands that cite Drive Like Jehu.
years.xp: Consequence collects two of them. At the Drive-In's Cedric Bixler-Zavala: "Drive Like Jehu were our strongest influences." Modest Mouse's Isaac Brock called them "one of my favorite all-time bands."

years.src: Consequence: The Strange Return of Drive Like Jehu
years.h: Trombino opens a doughnut shop, Donut Friend, in Los Angeles
years.p: Consequence reports a second location followed in 2019.

eras.title: The organ show
eras.text: A free afternoon with a pipe organ in San Diego turns into two years of festival dates.

years.cap: Drive Like Jehu with organist Dr. Carol Williams, Spreckels Organ Pavilion, San Diego, August 31, 2014
years.src: Wikipedia: Drive Like Jehu · setlist.fm: Drive Like Jehu at Spreckels Organ Pavilion · BrooklynVegan: Drive Like Jehu first show in 19 years · Consequence: The Strange Return of Drive Like Jehu
years.h: Drive Like Jehu return after 19 years, backed by a pipe organ
years.p: At San Diego's Spreckels Organ Pavilion, civic organist Dr. Carol Williams joins them for five songs. Trombino bought a drum kit for it.
years.xp:
The set was "Do You Compute," "Super Unison," "Sinews," "If It Kills You" and "Luau," with Rob Crow singing on "Luau." It was free and open to the public. Dang Nguyen, who co-owns Bar Pink with Reis and sits on the Spreckels Organ Society board, set it up.

Reis told the press why the organ appealed: "I especially love the way the low-end sound on the organ is so massive." Trombino had not owned a drum set since the breakup, according to Wikipedia.

Kennedy on why they did it at all, per Consequence: "We needed to know that we could do it."

years.cap: Drive Like Jehu at the Spreckels Organ Pavilion, San Diego
years.src: Wikipedia: Drive Like Jehu · mxdwn: Drive Like Jehu reunites for Coachella 2015 · Consequence: The Strange Return of Drive Like Jehu
years.h: The one-off turns into Coachella, twice
years.p: Casbah in San Diego on April 7 and 14, Pomona on the 8th, Coachella on April 11 and 18.
years.xp: Coachella announced the band in January 2015; mxdwn noted the August 2014 show had been expected to be a one-off. Consequence says the festival sets came to three songs in 40 minutes, since the songs run long.

years.cap: Rick Froberg on stage in San Diego
years.h: The reunion run ends in August 2016, after Iceland and Noise Pop
years.p: ATP Iceland in Keflavik on July 3, 2015, Treasure Island Music Festival on October 18, and Noise Pop in 2016 before the run wraps in August 2016.

eras.title: Froberg's art
eras.text: Rick Froberg dies in 2023, and his drawings get their own book.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rick Froberg · BrooklynVegan: Rick Froberg dead at 55 · Rolling Stone: Rick Froberg dead at 55 · Clash: Rick Froberg has died
years.h: Froberg dies at 55, and Reis tells fans on Instagram
years.p: "Rick passed away suddenly last night from natural causes," Reis wrote. The line above is from the same post.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and BrooklynVegan give his death as due to an undiagnosed heart condition, which BrooklynVegan attributes to a post by his girlfriend. Rolling Stone reports that shortly before his death he said the fifth Hot Snakes album was nearly finished.

Reis's post continued: "The only thing he loved more than art and rock n roll was his friends."

years.h: Akashic publishes Plenty for All, a book of Froberg's art
years.p: Pen and ink, linocuts, paintings and band art, per Wikipedia.
